_type.description: The component to render. "Header": A section heading. Renders as a bold title.; "Text": A run of text. Use for paragraphs, labels, or inline copy.; "Caption": Secondary, de-emphasized text under a primary element.; "Image": An image. Provide `src` and `alt` for accessibility. Put several images in a `Row` for a gallery, or a `sm` image beside text for a thumbnail.; "Divider": A horizontal rule between sections.; "Diagram": A diagram drawn from Mermaid source, such as a flowchart, a sequence of messages, or the states of a process. Keep it small and label the nodes in plain words.; "Map": Places on a map, such as the stops of a trip or locations to compare, with an optional route through them in order.; "Fact": A label/value pair, rendered as a key followed by its value. Use for compact metadata, and put an answer's key figures side by side in a `Row`.; "Button": A clickable button. Carries `_action` describing the side effect or resume value. Set `submit` to submit an ancestor Form/Card instead of firing `_action` on click.; "Select": A dropdown selector. Carries `_action` describing the on-select behavior.; "Input": A text input. Carries `_action` describing the on-submit behavior.; "DatePicker": A date, datetime, or time input. Carries `_action`, which runs once per committed value: a pick from the picker, or a typed value on blur or Enter.; "Checkbox": A checkbox with a label. Carries `_action` describing the on-change behavior.; "Slider": A numeric range control. Carries `_action` describing the committed value.; "RadioGroup": A group of mutually exclusive radio options. Carries `_action` describing the on-change behavior.; "CheckboxGroup": A group of checkbox options where any number can be checked. Set `progress` for a checklist the user works through. Carries `_action` describing the on-change behavior.; "Form": Wraps named child controls (Select/Input/Checkbox/RadioGroup/CheckboxGroup/DatePicker with a `name`). Carries `_action`; on submit it fires with every named control's value, keyed by `name`.; "Card": A module the reader scans or acts on, such as a summary, a checklist, a form, or one option in a comparison. It renders as a panel, so keep plain sections (a `Header` with `Text` or `Markdown`) outside cards, and do not wrap the whole answer in one card or nest cards. It takes on a framed surface when `background` is set, when `confirm`/`cancel` add a footer, or when it is a slot in a `Carousel`. Set `asForm` to collect named child control values on submit.; "Col": A vertical stack; children laid out top to bottom.; "Row": A horizontal row; children laid out left to right.; "Spacer": Empty space that pushes neighbors apart.; "Badge": A small labeled tag, e.g. for status or category.; "Box": A generic container for composition, e.g. a progress bar built from an outer track Box containing a partial-width fill Box. Size, radius, and background accept arbitrary values, so they render as inline styles rather than data-attribute hooks.; "Tabs": Panels the user switches between with tabs, one visible at a time. Use it for parallel content the user looks at one part at a time, such as options, plans, or days. Each child is one panel, usually a Col, labeled by the matching entry in `tabs`.; "ListView": A vertical list container. Wrap `ListViewItem` children as rows.; "ListViewItem": A row inside a ListView. Carries `_action` to make the whole row clickable and keyboard-activatable.; "Steps": Numbered steps to follow in order, such as instructions or a how-to guide. Each step has a short `title` saying what to do and an optional `detail` on how.; "Timeline": Events in time order, each with a time or date label, such as a schedule, an itinerary, or a history.; "Table": Tabular data. Provide `columns` and `rows`; each row is an array of cells matching the columns.; "Markdown": A markdown string. Rendered as-is by default; override this component for a full markdown renderer.; "Chart": A chart. `variant` selects bar, line, sparkline, or area rendering. Provide `data` for a single series, or `series` for multiple named series (`series` takes precedence over `data` when both are present). Set `stacked` to accumulate series values instead of overlaying them, and `showAxis`/`showLegend` to add y-axis ticks, x-axis point labels, and a legend.; "Citation": A source the answer draws on, shown as a card with its title and site that links to it. Use one per source.; "Alert": A highlighted message conveying urgency. `tone` drives the severity.; "Carousel": A horizontally scrollable group of `Card` children (max 10). Set `label` for an accessible name.; "Icon": A small line icon from the built-in set. `size` controls the rendered pixel size.

_key.description: Stable identity for this UI node. Use it for list items that may reorder.

anyOf.description: The text or number to display.
The fact value as text or a number.

Initial value: YYYY-MM-DD for date, HH:mm or HH:mm:ss with optional fraction of at most 9 digits for time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm with optional :ss and fraction of at most 9 digits for datetime. A datetime with Z or ±HH:mm is an instant, displayed in the viewer's time zone and submitted with the same offset and precision. A datetime without an offset is local and submitted unchanged. An empty datetime submits with the viewer's offset and seconds.
Series color (single-series mode only). One of `emphasis`, `secondary`, `alpha-70`, `white`, `white-70`, or `white-50`, matching Text's `color` tokens; other values have no visual effect.

src.description: Image URL, taken from a tool result or the user; never invent one.

round.description: Render as a circular avatar (fully rounded, cropped to a square).

flush.description: Whether the divider spans the full width with no inset.

code.description: Mermaid source, such as `flowchart LR` followed by `A[Order] --> B[Ship]`.

anyOf.description: A caption for the diagram, as text or a number.
Optional card title text or number.
The source's title as text or a number.

detail.description: A short note about the place.

route.description: Draw a line through the places in order.

anyOf.description: The fact label (key) as text or a number.
Label text or number next to the checkbox.
Accessible name as text or a number for the row of tabs.

block.description: Whether the button spans the full width.

submit.description: Render as a submit button for an ancestor Form/Card instead of a click button.

undoable.description: Delay the action with an undo control, for sends and other hard-to-reverse actions.

anyOf.description: Placeholder text or number shown when nothing is selected.
Field name used inside a Form.
Single-line input type. Values remain strings.
Temporal input type. Defaults to "date". Values remain strings.

multiline.description: Render a textarea instead of a single-line input; ignored when `inputType` is `"password"` or `"number"`.

anyOf.description: Minimum value: YYYY-MM-DD for date, HH:mm or HH:mm:ss with optional fraction of at most 9 digits for time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm with optional :ss and fraction of at most 9 digits for datetime. Datetimes with Z or ±HH:mm are converted to the viewer's time zone.

Maximum value: YYYY-MM-DD for date, HH:mm or HH:mm:ss with optional fraction of at most 9 digits for time, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm with optional :ss and fraction of at most 9 digits for datetime. Datetimes with Z or ±HH:mm are converted to the viewer's time zone.
Whether to render a checkbox or switch.

progress.description: Show how many options are checked, with a progress bar.

gap.description: Gap between children in 4px units. 0 to 8 is the supported range.

padding.description: Padding in 4px units (e.g. 2 = 8px). 0 to 8 is the supported range.

anyOf.description: Background color or gradient (any CSS background value). Setting this also switches the card's own text to white, since a custom background makes the card a tinted surface; children can still opt into a different color explicitly.
Background color or gradient (any CSS background value).

asForm.description: Render as a form; submitting it fires `confirm._action`, or the Card's own `_action` when `confirm` has none, with every named child control's value keyed by `name`.

confirm.description: Confirm button shown in the footer.

label.description: Footer button label text or number.

_action.description: Action fired when the button is activated.

type.description: The action type, resolved by the host's action registry.

cancel.description: Cancel button shown in the footer.

label.description: Footer button label text or number.

_action.description: Action fired when the button is activated.

type.description: The action type, resolved by the host's action registry.

radius.description: Corner radius; "full" is a pill/circle, a number is pixels.

tabs.description: Tab labels as text or numbers, one per child panel, in order.

title.description: What to do, in a few words, as text or a number.

detail.description: How to do it, or what to watch for, as text or a number.

time.description: When it happens, as the user should read it, such as `Day 1`, `6:00 pm`, or `1969`, as text or a number.

title.description: What happens, as text or a number.

detail.description: More about it, as text or a number.

kind.description: Format kind. `percent` takes a fraction, so 0.25 renders as 25%.

data.description: Data points for a single series.

series.description: Multiple named series; takes precedence over `data` when present.

label.description: Series label, shown in the legend.

color.description: Series color. One of `emphasis`, `secondary`, `alpha-70`, `white`, `white-70`, or `white-50`, matching Text's `color` tokens; other values have no visual effect.

stacked.description: Accumulate series values instead of overlaying them (bar and area variants; ignored for line and sparkline).

showAxis.description: Show y-axis ticks and x-axis point labels.

showLegend.description: Show a legend mapping each series to its color.

url.description: Link to the source; only http and https links open.

source.description: Where it comes from, such as a site or publication, as text or a number. Defaults to the link's domain.

snippet.description: A short quote or summary of what the source says, as text or a number.
